extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, empirical researchers, and practitioners studying patent litigation and injunctive relief
extracted.subtask_description: Hand-coded empirical analysis of contested permanent injunction decisions in U.S. district courts following eBay (May 2006–Dec 2013), including construction of a Decisions Dataset and a Patents Dataset with standardized coding rules and numerous binary/numeric variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions Dataset inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Contested permanent injunction decisions following eBay (May 15, 2006 through Dec. 31, 2013) were identified and included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded uncontested injunctions (e.g., default judgments or consented injunctions), preliminary injunctions, and cases involving design patents. Two cases counted as having two decisions when appropriate (e.g., multiple decisions on injunctive relief). Source lists included Patstats.org spreadsheet, Lex Machina searches, and Federal Trade Commission report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case identification via Lex Machina
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for searching Lex Machina: (1) selected 'Documents' tab; (2) search text 'permanent injunction' OR eBay; (3) selected 'Order re: Injunction' in 'Document Tags'; (4) selected 'Patent' in 'Case Types'; (5) reviewed entries for contested injunction decisions issued between May 15, 2006 and Dec. 31, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined multiple sources (Patstats spreadsheet, Lex Machina, FTC report) and updated Patstats document to include rulings to Dec. 31, 2013. Five FTC-listed cases were excluded for not meeting study criteria (e.g., default judgments, design patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for excluding uncontested injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncontested injunction decisions were excluded because counting them would likely skew the grant rate higher and they typically provide little illumination regarding why an injunction was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncontested injunctions are often granted with little or no discussion by the district court and thus are not informative for analyzing judicial reasoning about injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of preliminary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary injunction decisions were omitted because their procedural posture applies a distinct four-part test (likelihood of success on merits, likelihood of irreparable harm, balance of equities, public interest) and because preliminary injunctions are significantly less frequent than permanent injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Trebro Mfg. v. Firefly Equip. and Winter v. NRDC for the preliminary injunction test; empirical work suggests patentees obtain preliminary injunctions only rarely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-coding with standardized written coding instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each injunction decision was hand coded for a variety of information using standardized coding instructions. Student research assistants conducted initial drafts and the author personally reviewed and finalized coding for all variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written coding instructions were used to promote consistency and replicability; a copy of the author's written coding instructions is available upon request. Written rules mitigate subjectivity and improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLAINTIFF and DEFENDANT variables
rubrics_metrics.description: String variables were used for the name of the plaintiff [PLAINTIFF] and the defendant [DEFENDANT] in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple plaintiffs or defendants existed, only the first-named party was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: DISTRICT and DISTRICT_N variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The district court was initially recorded as a string variable [DISTRICT] using a three- or four-letter abbreviation consistent with PACER Case Locator; this string variable was then encoded into a separate categorical numeric variable [DISTRICT_N] for statistical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent abbreviations (per PACER) to allow reliable recoding into numeric categories for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: INJUNCTION variable definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [INJUNCTION] indicating whether a permanent injunction was granted for at least one claim of the patent(s)-in-suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat outcome as granted/denied at the decision level (binary) — study notes limitation that timing, duration, or scope of injunctions are not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: PATENTEE classification (8 categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each patent owner [PATENTEE] was coded into one of eight types: '(1) University; (2) Individual Inventor; (3) Large Patent Aggregator; (4) Failed Operating or Start-up Company; (5) Patent Holding Company; (6) Operating Company; (7) IP Holding Company Owned by Operating Company; and (8) Technology Development Company.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifications adopted from prior empirical work (Cotropia, Kesan & Schwartz); use complaint and public sources (e.g., patentee website) to classify. These categories capture differences such as PAEs vs operating companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: TECH (technological field) coding
rubrics_metrics.description: The technological field of the asserted patent(s) was coded into categories: (1) Computer Software; (2) Electronics; (3) Electrical; (4) Mechanical; (5) Chemical; (6) Biotechnology; (7) Drugs; (8) Medical Devices; and (9) Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories were modified from Allison, Lemley & Walker; used to analyze variation in injunction grant rates by technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: BUSMETHOD binary variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [BUSMETHOD] indicating whether the patent(s)-in-suit claimed a business method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple yes/no coding to capture business-method patents as a distinct class for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA (Hatch–Waxman) variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [ANDA] indicating whether the case involved a claim of infringement by a pharmaceutical manufacturer under the Hatch–Waxman Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statutory context (21 U.S.C. § 355(j); 35 U.S.C. § 271(e)) and the Federal Judicial Center's Patent Case Management Guide for guidance on classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding of eBay four factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The district court’s conclusions on each of the four eBay factors were coded: (1) irreparable harm [FACTOR1]; (2) inadequate remedy at law [FACTOR2]; (3) balance of hardships [FACTOR3]; and (4) the public interest would not be disserved by an injunction [FACTOR4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each factor recorded separately to analyze which factor(s) drive injunction grants; these are the canonical legal factors from eBay v. MercExchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: COMPETE variable definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [COMPETE] indicating whether the parties were classified as competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties classified as competitors if they competed in a product market at any time during the patent term. Licensing alone was insufficient to demonstrate competition. ANDA litigants intending to compete were classified as competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: LICENSE coding rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [LICENSE] indicating whether the patent holder had licensed or offered to license the patent(s)-in-suit to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive licenses by the patent owner to a co-plaintiff were excluded from being coded as licenses for this variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: COMPONENT variable (small component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [COMPONENT] coded whether the district court found that the patented invention was a 'small component' of the accused product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures district court reasoning that limited importance of patent to accused product may weigh against injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: WILLFUL infringement variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [WILLFUL] indicating whether the infringer willfully infringed the patent(s)-in-suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to capture potential relationship between willfulness findings and injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Dataset inclusion & duplication rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patents Dataset includes patents-in-suit from the injunction decisions: 392 separate U.S. patents (396 entries because four patents appear twice due to multiple lawsuits or multiple injunctive decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate patent entries are allowed when the same patent is subject to multiple contested injunction decisions or multiple decisions within the same case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-level numeric variables (ISSUE2INJUNCTION, CLAIMS, PRIORART, PARENT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent-level variables were hand coded: years between patent issuance and injunction decision [ISSUE2INJUNCTION] (numeric); total number of claims [CLAIMS] (numeric); number of prior art references cited by the patent [PRIORART] (numeric); number of predecessor (parent) applications [PARENT] (numeric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent applications include continuation and continuation-in-part applications; exclude foreign provisional and reissue/reexamination applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMALL entity coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary variable [SMALL] indicating whether the original patentee was a small entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small entity defined per 37 C.F.R. § 1.27(a) (individual, small business concern, or nonprofit) and entitles to fee reduction; coded as binary.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBER technology classification and forward citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Included NBER technology classification for each patent and forward citation counts as proxies for patent characteristics: total forward citations [FWDCITE] and average forward citations per year since issuance [FWDCITEPERYEAR].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NBER categories per Hall et al.; forward citations retrieved from Google Patents (Referenced By) as of July 2014. FWDCITEPERYEAR used to adjust for truncation due to future citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: selection effects and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Study limited to litigated court decisions; selection effects may bias results because tried cases are not a random sample, and parties tend to settle when standards clearly favor one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results are not representative of all patent disputes or all litigation; decisions include only cases where patentee filed suit and prevailed on liability, which occurs in only about a quarter of cases litigated to judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: reliance on published judicial opinions and potential circularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Content analysis limited by what opinions reveal; judicial opinions might selectively describe facts to justify outcomes (circularity), and reasoning may be unavailable if decisions or transcripts are sealed or not publicly accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealed opinions or unavailable transcripts can omit court reasoning; acknowledge potential bias from relying on published opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: appellate outcomes and binary outcome treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Study is limited to district court decisions and does not include outcomes or reasoning on appeal to the Federal Circuit; also treats permanent injunction decisions as a binary variable without considering timing, duration, or scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a district court injunction is vacated or reversed on appeal, that appellate outcome is not included in the Decisions Dataset; binary treatment may obscure nuanced remedial differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant rates reported (e.g., overall grant rate 72.5%); statistical significance testing used (Pearson’s chi-square, p-values), with mention of multiple testing correction (Bonferroni adjustment) where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: software grant-rate difference was statistically significant (p = 0.004) and remained so after Bonferroni adjustment across nine technology categories. Data analysis performed using Stata/IC 14.0.
